subject: [Retro Lab] Open actions — Sprint 1 Retro (Sprint 1)
body:
Sprint 1 Retro
Period: Sprint 1
Team: Chartswap
Archived: November 20, 2026
Open approved actions (6):
• ACT-0001 — Add mid-sprint dev–QA test-scope sync
  Teams: Dev Team, QA Team, Product Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0005 shows QA scope misalignment late in the cycle; FB-0003 shows bugs reaching QA too late. A fixed mid-sprint checkpoint lets QA confirm coverage and dev flag at-risk stories before the final handoff.
• ACT-0002 — Require two reviewers on every release-path PR
  Teams: Dev Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0006 calls for two reviewers on PRs. Making dual review mandatory on main and release branches spreads review load and catches issues before late-cycle QA churn.
• ACT-0003 — Timebox daily standups to 15 minutes
  Teams: Dev Team, Management Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0004 reports dailies running too long. A 15-minute cap with a parking-lot channel for deep dives keeps ceremony discipline without losing blocker visibility.
• ACT-0004 — Introduce a pre-QA merge checklist
  Teams: Dev Team, QA Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0003 highlights late bugs handed to QA. A short checklist before the QA queue reduces rework at the end of the sprint.
• ACT-0005 — Align acceptance criteria with QA during sprint planning
  Teams: QA Team, Product Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0005 flags test-scope gaps. Reviewing acceptance criteria with QA when stories are committed keeps expected coverage explicit from day one.
• ACT-0006 — Document what worked in the recent release
  Teams: Dev Team, Ops Team | Target: 2026-11-20
  FB-0001 and FB-0002 credit successful release delivery. Capturing the practices that worked gives the team a repeatable playbook for the next cycle.
Themes: Successful release delivery: The team reported strong collaboration during release week and delivered the milestone on the planned date. Late-cycle quality gaps: A recurring concern is that many bugs reached QA late in the sprint; feedback also points toward earlier QA alignment on test scope before formal testing. Process discipline (ceremonies and reviews): Daily syncs frequently ran over schedule, and the team raised ideas to tighten pull-request review before merge.
—
Generated by Retrospective Lab. Replies are not monitored.
